Standing and pickup correction

Unused arms now retain the provider elbow and wrist pose. A small outward shoulder turn keeps the hands and sleeves clear of the trousers. The pickup uses the shared instrument stand. Its tray is within reach. The tool stays on the tray until the action ends, then attaches near the palm. The body returns upright after pickup.

The mesh surface check found no hand or forearm vertices more than 1 mm inside the leg surfaces in all six standing dispositions. The pickup contact pose also passed this check. The current rig has no finger joints, so the hand does not close around the tool.

125 unit tests and both builds pass. Earlier captures below show prior revisions.

Correction: reversed limb controls

The first proof missed a code error. The game used the wrong local X direction for both hand targets and the elbow and knee bend controls. This pulled left limbs toward the right side and right limbs toward the left side. The controls now use one shared anatomical side map.

The original and processed meshes have the correct arm and leg weights. The proof now has a Source selector. Choose Original RUN clip to play the provider mesh, skeleton, and animation without game pose controls. Choose Game motion to inspect the correction. No model was regenerated.

The new browser regression checks the actual elbow, hand, and knee positions in model coordinates. It passed during standing and 20 walking samples. The earlier captures below predate this correction.

Changes in the playable

Walking uses short, unequal steps. One foot stays planted while the other moves. The body turns toward its path. The root has no vertical bounce. His arms stay near his body during travel. He lowers his hips to treat the patient. During a lift, both hands and his body rise with the support.

Object shapes use thicker edges and layered surfaces. The cabinet, screen, lamp, lantern, door, and instrument tray use the same revised models in the proof and game.

Checks and limits

The browser walk check measured less than 0.01 mm of foot target error and stance drift. Pause kept the pose fixed. A 57-second check of the built proof crossed the room and returned to the patient. Foot target error remained below 0.01 mm. The playable rehearsal passed the cancelled lift, recovery, exposure, extraction, closure, and dressing checks. It produced no page errors.

The proof extends action times for inspection. It does not test live model decisions or the timing of remote room actions. The current rig has no finger joints. It can place the hands but cannot close individual fingers around an object.

Run locally

From games/still-warm, run npm run proof. Open the local viewer. It needs no RUN sign-in and makes no model calls. The game still uses port 4318.

Run npm run proof:build to create dist-proof/. Serve that directory through HTTP. The decoder and mesh files are local.

Captures show the real WebGL output. No assets were generated for this pass. The interactive proof uses a separate static server. The RUN Playground server is not shared.
